title: Updates: open terminals come back on their own after an update, and the update prompt warns first
story: Updating Maestro no longer just warns that open terminals will close: the prompt says they will close and come back, with the three points from the crash-recovery prototype (scene 3). After the update restart they come back on their own with no question. This replaces the old 'Close all terminals?' warning; before, the start after an update showed the 'Maestro stopped unexpectedly' offer.

checks.criterion: With terminals open, the prompt shows the count and three points; Not now changes nothing
checks.steps: On a build older than the latest release, open a project with one Claude and one plain terminal; click Download and Install on the update toast; click Not now; click Download and Install again.
checks.expected: A dialog 'Update Maestro to <version>?' saying 'Your 2 open terminals will close and come back after the update.' with three points and buttons Not now / Update and restart; after Not now nothing installs and the toast stays.

checks.criterion: With no terminals, the download starts straight away
checks.steps: Close every terminal, then click Download and Install.

checks.criterion: After the update restart, terminals come back with no dialog, once
checks.steps: Open a Claude terminal with one message, a plain shell and a parked terminal; Download and Install, Update and restart; after it is back, close Maestro normally and start again.
checks.expected: No 'stopped unexpectedly' dialog; all three come back (Claude continues, shell empty with the amber line, parked one on the shelf); nothing is offered after the normal restart.
